subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: Should a matched Signal edit append structured correction context, or should OpenClaw add a generic session API that replaces the original inbound transcript entry?
rationale: The parser and plugin boundary are clear, but replacement changes persisted session history and projections, while append-only correction changes prompt and context semantics; repository evidence does not establish which permanent product contract maintainers want.

options.title: Structured correction event
options.body: Keep distinct edit-event and target identities, append explicit corrected context, and suppress non-mentioned group edit replies without rewriting prior transcript state.

options.title: Generic transcript replacement
options.body: Design a core session-state mutation API and use it to replace the original inbound entry across storage and projections.

options.title: Marker-only behavior
options.body: Prefix edited content and otherwise retain ordinary dispatch, accepting that duplicate context and responses remain possible.

recommendation.title: Structured correction event
recommendation.body: Keep distinct edit-event and target identities, append explicit corrected context, and suppress non-mentioned group edit replies without rewriting prior transcript state.

likelyOwner.reason: The original and sustained Signal inbound history plus adjacent context and runtime ownership make this the best available decision route.
